name: 1936 S. Michigan Avenue — Second Presbyterian Church (district draft; refined by T-1942)

grade.why: Pictured: a picture on the Images tab shows it.

documented_range.note: The rebuilt church was rededicated in November 1901 (Chicago Tribune, 10 November 1901) and stands today; the draft claims the 1904 target.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body (u -32.340, v 5.960 m from the building's front and southernmost faces), set from the corner at local (1128.75, -3461.64): Michigan Avenue's centre is the e1871 terrain box's reading at 16th Street (E +1136.7), carried south on the bearing of Indiana Avenue's measured east line; its west line is 10.06 m out (the 66 ft every street on the committed sheets prints; Michigan's own width is not read here), and the church's east face stands a reconstructed 3.0 m behind it, as the photograph's lawn strip shows; the south face stands 3.0 m behind East Twentieth Street's measured north line (data/street_grid/1904.json). Good to a few metres. Rotation -0.572 degrees squares the plan to the avenue.
placement.symbolic_location: 1936 S. Michigan Avenue, the north-west corner of Michigan Avenue and East Twentieth Street, west of every committed Sanborn sheet.

footprint.note: The building's whole plan, the nave, the parish hall and the north aisle range as HABS IL-328 sheet 2 draws them, buttresses and the tower's projection left off, so the walls a visitor meets and the ground the context's stand-ins give way to are the church's own; the main body (the nave and narthex, 32.3 x 21.8 m) is draft_plan's first rectangle.

stories.note: Three draft storeys of 4.6 m over a 0.9 m floor stand the walls to the 14.7 m eave the 1901 cut shows against the nave's ridge; a church has no storeys, and the count only sets the wall height and the rows of openings.

construction.note: Stone: the rock-faced ashlar of the photograph and the 1901 cut, drawn in stone on HABS IL-328's elevations.

parts.from: the nave with its east narthex, chancel arch to the east wall (HABS IL-328 sheet 2, read at the feet bar (42.3 px/m on the library copy), north up)
the parish hall across the west end with the chancel and stair rooms beside it, its gable to 20th Street (HABS IL-328 sheet 2, read at the feet bar (42.3 px/m on the library copy), north up)
the north aisle range along the nave (HABS IL-328 sheet 2, read at the feet bar (42.3 px/m on the library copy), north up)

draft_plan.note: Three rectangles read off HABS IL-328 sheet 2 at its feet bar (the metric bar disagrees by 22 %; the pews' 0.92 m spacing settles which is right): the nave, the parish hall with the chancel rooms beside it, and the north aisle range. The narthex, vestibule and buttresses fold into the rectangles.

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the site row: The nave's ridge stands at HABS sheet 4's 87'-8 1/4" (26.7 m: a 48-degree gable over the 21.8 m nave) and the hall's gable at its 80'-1" (24.4 m: 50 degrees over 16.2 m). The tower is HABS sheet 2's 7.9 m square at the south-east corner; its masonry to about 38 m and its spire about 16 m above are proportions read off Sloan's photograph against the nave's ridge (upper figures: the tower stands nearer the camera). Openings are the draft's sash in rows, not the church's lancets, rose and great window, which are T-1942's. The seed 169477518 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-district-edges-2982.

draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: Second Presbyterian Church (James Renwick, 1872-1874), gutted by fire in March 1900 and rededicated in November 1901 inside its surviving walls and tower (Chicago Tribune, 10 November 1901).

citations.citation: "Second Presbyterian Church, Open Today" [halftone of the reconstructed church, with caption]. Chicago Sunday Tribune, 10 November 1901 (vol. 60 no. 313).

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2982, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1942 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the rules' site row (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-district-edges-2982). The church stands on Michigan Avenue at 20th Street, west of the three committed Sanborn sheets, so it is drafted from HABS IL-328's measured plan and south elevation and placed on the 1904 grid's measured lines. Its 1904 tower state is the full spire: the 1901 Tribune cut and Sloan's photograph (1901-1925) both show it, and it was lost in 1929.
